nodes.What it is: A camera turns 3D points into 2D pixels through a lens. The pinhole model, focal length, principal point and lens distortion describe this mapping, so code can go from pixels back to rays in the world.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Mature theory; still the base of every 3D perception pipeline. Learned models (VGGT, Depth Anything 3) now also predict camera parameters from images. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Textbook authors (Szeliski; Hartley & Zisserman; Corke); OpenCV community

nodes.What it is: Calibration measures a camera's internal parameters and where it sits relative to the robot. You show a checkerboard or ChArUco board from many angles and solve for the parameters; hand-eye calibration links camera frame and gripper frame.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Standard tooling exists (OpenCV, ROS camera_calibration, Kalibr for camera-IMU). Low-cost arm demos such as Google's SO-101 pointing sample still rely on a ChArUco homography step. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: ETH Zurich ASL (Kalibr); OpenCV; ROS image_pipeline maintainers

nodes.What it is: Before deep learning, robots found edges, corners, colors and keypoints with hand-written filters. Matching keypoints between images gives motion and 3D structure, and simple color thresholds are still the fastest way to get a first demo.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Still used for fast, explainable baselines and in SLAM front-ends; learned matchers compete for hard cases. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Fiducials are printed black-and-white square codes that software detects reliably and uses to compute the 6D pose of the tag. They are the quickest way to give a robot accurate object or camera positions without training a model.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Mature and widely used for ground truth, calibration and docking; AprilTag 3 library is the open reference. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: University of Michigan APRIL Lab; OpenCV ArUco module

nodes.What it is: Depth cameras give a distance for each pixel. Stereo cameras compare two views (triangulation), active cameras add a projected IR pattern or time-of-flight light. Knowing their noise and failure cases (shiny, transparent, dark surfaces) is essential.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Commodity RGB-D cameras (OAK-D, ZED, RealSense) are standard; learned stereo such as FoundationStereo (2025) claims strong zero-shot matching. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: A point cloud is a list of 3D points from a depth camera or LiDAR. Typical steps are downsampling, removing outliers, finding the table plane, clustering objects and aligning two clouds (ICP registration).
nodes.Prerequisites: Stereo & RGB-D depth sensing; rigid transforms
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Open3D and PCL are the standard libraries; learned 3D networks sit on top of the same preprocessing. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: A detector draws boxes and class labels around objects in each image. Models such as YOLO run in real time on a laptop GPU or edge board and can be fine-tuned on a few hundred labeled images of your own objects.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Ultralytics ships YOLO11 (2024) and YOLO26, with YOLO27 announced as 'coming soon' on its docs; RT-DETR offers a transformer alternative. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Segmentation labels the exact pixels of each object, not just a box. Meta's Segment Anything models cut out any object from a click, box or (SAM 3) a short text phrase, and track masks through video.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: SAM 2 (2024) added video memory; SAM 3 (Nov 2025, ICLR 2026) adds promptable concept segmentation from noun phrases or exemplars and is open-sourced. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Meta (FAIR / Meta Superintelligence Labs); IDEA Research (Grounded-SAM-2)

nodes.What it is: Tracking keeps the same ID on each object across frames, so a robot knows 'this is still the same cup'. Most trackers link detector boxes over time with motion prediction (Kalman filter) and matching.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Tracking-by-detection (ByteTrack, BoxMOT collection) remains the practical default; SAM 2/3 offer mask-level tracking. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: ByteTrack authors; BoxMOT maintainers; Ultralytics tracking mode

nodes.What it is: A neural network guesses depth from a single ordinary image. Recent models output metric depth (in meters) good enough for rough obstacle maps and for replacing a depth camera in cheap setups, though not for precise grasping.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Depth Anything V2 (2024), Apple Depth Pro (2024, metric) and Depth Anything 3 (Nov 2025, any-view geometry) are open; FetchBot (CoRL 2025) uses predicted depth for sim-to-real. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: ByteDance Seed / HKU (Depth Anything); Apple ML Research (Depth Pro)

nodes.What it is: Pose trackers find body joints or the 21 keypoints of a hand in video. Robots use them for gesture commands, safety zones and to retarget human hand motion into robot teleoperation or demonstrations.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Google MediaPipe Hand/Pose Landmarker run in real time on CPU/phone; industrial cobot surveys list gesture recognition and safety monitoring as core perception tasks. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Google AI Edge (MediaPipe); Ultralytics pose models

nodes.What it is: LiDAR measures distance with laser pulses and gives a precise 3D point cloud around the robot. 3D detectors find cars, people or boxes as 3D boxes in these clouds, as in autonomous driving datasets like KITTI.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: OpenPCDet is a common open toolbox; low-cost hybrid-solid LiDARs (Livox Mid-360) target mobile robots. Multi-sensor fusion is an active embodied-AI research area. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Open-vocabulary detectors find objects from any text you type ('the red mug'), without retraining on fixed classes. They link language models and vision so a robot can be told what to look for.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Grounding DINO (2023), OWLv2 (2023), Florence-2 and SAM 3 concept prompts are open; Grounded-SAM-2 chains detection, segmentation and tracking. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Foundation vision backbones are networks pretrained on huge image sets without labels. Their features describe image patches so well that a small head can do depth, segmentation or correspondence, and many robot policies use them as their 'eyes'.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DINOv2 (2023) is widely reused; Depth Anything 3 uses a plain DINO encoder as backbone. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Point trackers follow any chosen pixel through a video, even through occlusion. Robotics uses them to turn human or robot videos into motion data and to measure how objects move.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: CoTracker3 (Meta, 2024) and TAPIR (DeepMind) are open; used to extract motion from videos for robot learning. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: New transformer models take a few ordinary photos and directly output 3D points and camera poses in one pass, replacing slow classical photogrammetry. This gives robots quick 3D models of scenes from cheap cameras.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DUSt3R (2023), VGGT (2025, CVPR 2025 Best Paper Award) and Depth Anything 3 (2025, reports +35.7% camera-pose accuracy over VGGT on its benchmark). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: NAVER LABS Europe (DUSt3R, Grenoble); Oxford VGG & Meta (VGGT); ByteDance Seed (DA3)

nodes.What it is: NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting build photo-realistic, viewable 3D scenes from many photos. Robotics uses them for digital twins, simulation assets and maps that can be rendered from new viewpoints.
nodes.Prerequisites: Camera models; calibration; GPU programming basics helpful
nodes.Frontier state 2026: 3DGS (Inria, 2023) became standard; nerfstudio and gsplat are open toolkits; 2025-2026 work extends splats to SLAM, event cameras and articulated objects (ScrewSplat, CoRL 2025). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Inria GRAPHDECO; nerfstudio (UC Berkeley); research labs

nodes.What it is: A 3D scene graph stores the objects in a room, where they are and how they relate ('cup on table'), with language labels from foundation models. Robots query it with text to find and fetch things.
nodes.Prerequisites: Open-vocabulary detection; point clouds; RGB-D sensing
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ConceptGraphs (2023) and OK-Robot (2024) show open-knowledge pick-and-drop in homes; surveys (2025) frame 3D foundation models as possible unified representation. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Large vision-language models answer questions about images, point to objects and estimate progress, acting as a high-level 'brain' for a robot. They turn a camera image plus a sentence into coordinates or plans.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5 (Sept 2025) is marketed for pointing, detection and success detection via API; Google publishes an SO-101 pointing sample. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Event cameras report per-pixel brightness changes asynchronously with microsecond latency instead of full frames. They handle fast motion and extreme lighting where normal cameras blur, but need new algorithms.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Active research (event SLAM survey in IJCV 2026, event-based Gaussian splatting); Prophesee (Paris) ships sensors and the Metavision SDK. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

top3.justification: Accessibility 5, immediate visual demos, cheap webcam or sim start, and reused by sorting, tracking and pan-tilt projects; matches the team's AI skills.

Very fast language-to-pointing demo on the existing SO-101 via a public Google sample; high wow and ecosystem relevance (VLA/embodied reasoning trend). API cost unknown, so pair with the open-model comparison project.
Open models (Grounding DINO, OWLv2, SAM 3) give text-driven perception without training, near-zero hardware cost, and feed language-commanded manipulation projects.
